title: The Hunter Who Buried Spider-Man Alive
question: Why bury Spider-Man and take his place?

sources.title: Marvel: Kraven history
sources.excerpt: The hunter impersonates Peter, defeats Vermin, faces the escaped hero, interrupts Vermin, leaves a confession and dies by suicide. The burial causes lingering trauma.

sources.title: Marvel: Spider-Man stories by decade
sources.excerpt: The 1987 six-part Last Hunt has Kraven shoot and bury Peter, wear a cloth black suit and hunt Vermin; Peter emerges after two weeks.

sources.title: Marvel: Web of Spider-Man #32
sources.excerpt: The November 1987 issue shows Peter emerging and learning his impersonator has been active for two weeks.

sources.title: Marvel: Last Hunt reading order
sources.excerpt: Web of Spider-Man #31–32, Amazing Spider-Man #293–294 and Spectacular Spider-Man #131–132. The hunter wants to prove his mastery by taking Peter’s place.

claims.text: Kraven shot Peter, buried him alive, and wore a cloth version of the black Spider-Man suit in the 1987 six-part Last Hunt.
Peter was buried for two weeks in a state simulating death before climbing free.
Kraven intended to prove his mastery over Spider-Man by taking his place.
Kraven became a vicious vigilante; newspapers reported that Spider-Man had gone berserk.
Kraven defeated Vermin alone, where Spider-Man had previously needed Captain America’s help.
Peter confronted Kraven after escaping. Kraven accepted the assault and claimed victory rather than fighting back.
Kraven released Vermin against Peter, then stopped him before he killed Peter. Peter pursued Vermin.
Kraven left a confession and died by suicide. Peter’s living burial left lingering trauma.

notes: 1987 comics continuity, not the Kraven film or a game. Indexed official Marvel recaps and issue metadata reviewed; direct character/catalog pages returned 403. Full issues not read. Physical staging is illustrative. No injury, gunshot impact or suicide method is reenacted. Source cover is a local-review copyrighted image.
